name: assert
signature:
assert(cond)
assert(cond, msg, A1, ...)
assert(cond, errID, msg, A1, ...)
assert(observed, expected)
assert(observed, expected, tol)
summary: Raises an error when a condition is false or, in Octave's form, when an observed value doesn't match the expected one (within a tolerance).

examples.expected:
ASSERT errors for:  assert (cond,expected,tol)

  Location  |  Observed  |  Expected  |  Reason
    (3)           3            4         Abs err 1 exceeds tol 0 by 1

examples.code:
x = -1;
assert(x > 0, 'x must be positive, not %d', x)

differs: MATLAB has no assert(observed, expected, tol): that form follows Octave 11.1.
Octave's error header quotes the call's own text (assert (([1, 2, 3]),([1, 2, 4]))); Sagebrush writes assert (cond,expected,tol), as Octave does inside cells and structs.
When the first argument is a number or logical and the second is text, it is MATLAB's condition and message: assert(1, 'a') passes, where Octave compares 1 with 'a' and fails.
A failing condition alone gives MATLAB's Assertion failed., not Octave's assert (cond) failed.
